ledger.claim: The deviation is outside tolerance and the tolerance rows of the refund matrix cannot dispose of this case. POL-RD-22 fixes the deviation on the platform's recorded distances: trip_record.actual_distance_km (10.9 km) minus trip_record.optimal_distance_km (9.6 km) = 1.30 km, or 13.5% of the recommended route. That is more than the 1.0 km tolerance the same clause sets, and POL-RD-22 is explicit that the sparse GPS trace (9.226 km) is not used to re-measure the distance because it understates a route's length. So no 'within tolerance' outcome is available and the rider is 1.30 km of metered travel out of pocket.

The reroute is corroborated in time and place, and the rider paid for it. The trip events record the vehicle leaving the recommended route at the KPE / MacPherson Road exit at 21:22:26 and rejoining at Hougang Avenue 3 / Upper Paya Lebar Road at 21:34:06 — 11 minutes 40 seconds off the recommended route — and the driver-device trace shows consecutive fixes along MacPherson Road and Upper Paya Lebar Road across exactly that window. The fare ledger then charged the full 10.9 km travelled, including the excess, at 0.72 SGD per km.

The rider's case does not rest on want of notice: the driver's MSG-05014-003 (21:19:56, read 21:20:23, answered 21:20:41) preceded the 21:22:26 deviation, so POL-RD-21's notice limb is met on the chat log and no call recording is needed. The case rests on the fact that the notice produced no agreement. POL-RD-21 makes a deviation 'agreed' only where the chat log or a call recording confirms the rider's acknowledgment. The only acknowledgment on record is MSG-05014-004, and EV-CHAT-05014 is IMPAIRED — issue code LANGUAGE_AMBIGUITY, weight_multiplier 0.85 — because, as the admissibility note records, the message 'mixes assent with a condition on the fare'. 'aiyo can meh... ok lor whatever u say but dun charge me more ah' is conditional acquiescence to a driver who had already committed to the exit, not the confirmation of acknowledgment POL-RD-21 requires; and the condition was not honoured, since the rider was charged the full 10.9 km. Row (a) of POL-RD-24, which requires that the rider agreed, is therefore not made out.

Traffic justification is not established on the artifact's own record. POL-RD-23 justifies a reroute only where traffic data for the recommended route segment at the trip time shows congestion, an incident or a closure — a TRAFFIC_ADVISORY that intersects the recommended route and overlaps the trip window. EV-ADVIS-05014-01's derived block records overlaps_trip_window as true but leaves intersects_route and justifies_reroute null, with the stated reason that 'the record does not say whether this advisory lies on the recommended route'. The window overlap is established; the intersection with the recommended route is not, and POL-RD-23's second sentence provides that a driver's assertion of traffic without such data does not justify the reroute. On the rider's case the reroute is not traffic-justified and, the deviation being over 1 km, POL-RD-24(d) applies: the excess distance fare is refunded in full.

The sum in issue is fixed by the policy and the rider presses for exactly that. POL-RD-24 defines the excess distance fare as the deviation distance times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, without surge, rounded to the cent: 1.30 km x 0.72 SGD = 0.94 SGD, and the fare ledger's own derived money block records that figure. The rider asks the return of $4.20; the refund matrix provides the excess distance fare and nothing more, so the claim is pressed for the 0.94 SGD the policy allows, which is the amount that would move the rider back to the position of the recommended route.

If the judge instead finds the reroute traffic-justified, no row of POL-RD-24 fits and the case must be escalated. Row (b) needs the rider to have been uninformed, and she was informed; row (a) needs her to have agreed, and on EV-CHAT-05014 (IMPAIRED, LANGUAGE_AMBIGUITY, weight 0.85) her reply was at best conditional. POL-RD-24 provides that a case fitting no row — its own example being 'informed but the rider objected' — is escalated under POL-GEN-26. That is a rider-safe outcome: an escalated amount is held rather than finally collected, and the open question goes to a human reviewer.

Any ruling for the driver on this file is also barred at the confidence stage. The fact on which a NO_ACTION ruling under POL-RD-24(a) turns — the rider's acknowledgment — is carried by one artifact only, EV-CHAT-05014, at weight_multiplier 0.85 (issue code LANGUAGE_AMBIGUITY). POL-GEN-02(2) forbids confidence above the lowest weight among the artifacts carrying the deciding fact, so confidence on that fact is capped at 0.85, and this file's required confidence is 0.95: the rider's profile carries fraud_flags of 1, a field POL-GEN-22 names, which raises the bar 'whatever the value'. No NO_ACTION ruling can therefore stand (POL-RD-25), and the present charge cannot be closed against the rider on this record.

The reroute was traffic-justified under POL-RD-23. EV-ADVIS-05014-01 is an LTA ACCIDENT advisory on the Kallang-Paya Lebar Expressway (KPE) towards TPE, after the MacPherson Road exit, valid from 21:06:05 to 22:16:05 on 3 September 2026, which covers the whole trip window (started 21:16:05, ended 21:38:05). ACCIDENT is an admissible incident type in the policy's traffic-justification vocabulary, so it is the kind of condition that justifies a reroute. The advised road is the recommended route itself: the trip record's recommended route is Stadium Boulevard, KPE, Hougang Avenue 3, Hougang Avenue 10, and the advisory sits on the KPE towards TPE after the MacPherson Road exit - the very point at which the trip record shows the vehicle leaving the route (route_deviation_detected at 21:22:26, 'KPE / MacPherson Road exit'). On the advisory's own road, direction and location fields it therefore intersects the recommended route and overlaps the trip window. The driver's assertion is not bare: it is corroborated by third-party traffic data retrieved by the platform, not supplied by him.

The driver gave the rider notice before the deviation, which is what POL-RD-21 requires. He messaged at 21:19:56 (MSG-05014-003: 'Accident on KPE ahead, I exit MacPherson then go Upper Paya Lebar, can?'), the rider read it at 21:20:23, and the route_deviation_detected event is timestamped 21:22:26 - so the message was sent and read before the point of deviation, and it gave a brief reason, which POL-RD-21 says is enough. No call recording is needed because the notice was given by in-app chat. I disclose that EV-CHAT-05014 is IMPAIRED: issue code LANGUAGE_AMBIGUITY fired and its weight_multiplier is 0.85. That impairment, on its own issue detail, attaches to the rider's reply (MSG-05014-004), not to the fact that the driver's notice (MSG-05014-003) was sent and read before the deviation.

The rider acknowledged the deviation, so it is an agreed deviation under POL-RD-21. Her reply at 21:20:41 (MSG-05014-004, 'aiyo can meh... ok lor whatever u say but dun charge me more ah') yields the routing decision to the driver - 'ok lor whatever u say' - and the trailing 'dun charge me more' is a statement about the fare, not a refusal of the reroute. Her own claim text is to the same effect: she says she told him not to charge her more, which confirms she received the notice and answered on the money, not with a demand to stay on the KPE. The driver's contemporaneous statement ('I asked the passenger and she said ok') matches the chat. I do not present this reply as clean evidence: EV-CHAT-05014 is IMPAIRED, issue code LANGUAGE_AMBIGUITY, weight 0.85, because the message mixes assent with a fare condition. Read at 0.85 it still shows acknowledgment of the reroute; the ambiguity is about the fare, and the fare question is answered by the matrix below, not by POL-RD-21.

On those facts exactly one row of POL-RD-24 applies: row (a) - traffic-justified, rider informed and agreed, deviation over 1 km - and row (a) gives no refund (NO_ACTION). The deviation is over tolerance: 10.9 km actual less 9.6 km recommended is 1.30 km, above POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance, and POL-RD-22 fixes that measurement on the platform's recorded distances, not on the 9.226 km sparse GPS trace. The metered fare of 16.97 SGD therefore stands. NO_ACTION is party-relative under POL-GEN-03: the rider is the filer, and the payments ledger shows payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the present state that POL-GEN-03 preserves is one in which the driver keeps the fare and no money moves.

If the judge reads 'dun charge me more ah' as an objection rather than assent, the case fits none of POL-RD-24's rows - POL-RD-24 names 'informed but the rider objected' as exactly the case that fits no row - and the outcome is escalation under POL-GEN-26, not a refund. On escalation no monetary outcome issues and the amount is held (POL-GEN-03). The rider's reply is the only artifact that carries her state of mind, and it is IMPAIRED (LANGUAGE_AMBIGUITY, weight 0.85); so even on the reading least favourable to the driver, the alternative to NO_ACTION is a held fare, never a payment back to the rider.

A final AI ruling of NO_ACTION cannot be entered on the agreement question in any event, so the holding outcome is human review, which is still no refund. The rider's profile carries fraud_flags of 1 (rider_profile.fraud_flags), so POL-GEN-22 requires a confidence of 0.95 whatever the value; and because the only artifact carrying the rider's reply is EV-CHAT-05014 at weight 0.85, POL-GEN-02(2) caps the judge's confidence on that fact at 0.85. Below the required confidence, POL-RD-25 sends the route-deviation ruling to human review. Fraud_flags is cited only for POL-GEN-22, which is the rule that names it, and it does not decide this trip.

Under POL-RD-24 the only refund the matrix ever awards here is the excess distance fare - deviation distance times fare_breakdown.per_km_rate_sgd, without surge, rounded to the cent: 1.30 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 0.94 SGD. That is the ceiling even on the rider's best rows (b) or (d), and neither of those rows fits in any case: the reroute was traffic-justified (row (d) is out) and the rider was informed before the deviation (row (b), which requires that she was not informed, is out). Partial refund cannot exceed 0.94 SGD; NO_ACTION and escalation return nothing to the rider at all.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this route-deviation case goes to a human reviewer, and no money moves on it now. The SGD 16.97 metered fare stays charged (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00) and is held; nothing is refunded to the rider at this stage. Here is why.

What the record settles.
(1) The deviation. The trip ran 10.9 km against a recommended 9.6 km, so the deviation is 1.30 km, over POL-RD-22's 1.0 km tolerance. POL-RD-22 fixes that on the platform's recorded distances (EV-TRIP-05014, weight 1.0, complete), not on the sparse 9.226 km trace, so no 'within tolerance' outcome is available. The rider is right on this point.
(2) Notice. The driver's in-app message MSG-05014-003 was sent at 21:19:56 and read at 21:20:23, before the vehicle left the route at 21:22:26, and it gave a brief reason. POL-RD-21's notice limb is met by the chat, and no call recording is needed. The driver is right on this point, and the rider accepts it.
(3) Traffic justification. I find the LTA advisory EV-ADVIS-05014-01 intersects the recommended route, so POL-RD-23 is satisfied. It is an ACCIDENT (an admissible incident type) on the KPE towards TPE after the MacPherson Road exit, valid 21:06-22:16, which covers the trip window 21:16-21:38. The recommended route runs on the KPE (Stadium Boulevard, KPE, Hougang Avenue 3, Hougang Avenue 10), and the trip record shows the vehicle leaving that route at exactly the KPE / MacPherson Road exit (21:22:26) while 'recommended KPE' - so the recommended route continues on the KPE past that exit, which is precisely where the advisory sits. The rider's contrary argument, that intersection is not established because the artifact's derived field is null, is rejected: that field is left for me to decide from the advisory's road, direction and location against the trip, and they line up. This matters because it rules out POL-RD-24 rows (d) and (e) and with them the rider's claim that the excess distance fare is refundable as of right.

What the record does not settle - the open question.
(4) Whether the rider agreed. POL-RD-24(a) (no refund) needs the deviation to have been both notified and agreed, and POL-RD-21 makes it 'agreed' only where the chat log confirms the rider's acknowledgment. The only acknowledgment on record is MSG-05014-004 (21:20:41): 'aiyo can meh... ok lor whatever u say but dun charge me more ah'. That chat log, EV-CHAT-05014, is IMPAIRED: issue code LANGUAGE_AMBIGUITY, weight_multiplier 0.85, because the message mixes assent with a condition on the fare. It therefore does not cleanly confirm acknowledgment. Read one way the rider yielded the routing choice to the driver; read the other she attached a fare condition she says was broken. Row (a) is not made out, row (b) fails because she was in fact informed, and no other row of POL-RD-24 fits - which is the case POL-RD-24 sends to human review under POL-GEN-26. The driver's read of the message as plain acceptance, and the rider's read of it as an objection, are each more than this record can establish.
(5) Confidence. My confidence may not exceed the weight of the artifact carrying that decisive fact (POL-GEN-02(2)): the rider's acknowledgment/objection is carried only by EV-CHAT-05014 at 0.85, and the driver's counterparty statement (self-serving, made the next day) carries no weight and cannot lift it. Because the rider's profile carries fraud_flags of 1, POL-GEN-22 fixes the required confidence at 0.95 whatever the value, and POL-RD-25 will not let a route-deviation ruling stand below it. So even had I read the reply as assent, a NO_ACTION ruling could not stand; the driver's alternative argument that the outcome is at most 'no refund' is therefore only half right - it is human review, not a final no-action.

Money and referrals. The rider asks 4.20 SGD; the most POL-RD-24 can ever award on these facts is the excess distance fare, 1.30 km x 0.72 SGD/km = 0.94 SGD without surge (EV-FARE-05014's own derived figure), but on an escalation no amount is refunded or newly collected - the fare is held. No referral is added: no clause in this category produces one.

Question for the reviewer: whether MSG-05014-004 was an agreement to the reroute or an objection to it, and, if conditional, whether 'dun charge me more ah' should leave the metered fare as charged or move it.

The judge was asked 4 times on the same inputs and 3 of the 4 drafts agreed on this ruling, so it is carried, not unanimous (vote agreement 0.75).
